utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Case number IT-98-34-A, the Prosecutor versus Mladen Naletilic and Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I now call for the appearances for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KIND
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, my name is Marie-Ursula Kind, appearing today together with Senior Appeals Counsel, Norman Farrell and Ms. Lourdes Galicia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Mr. Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Zelimir Par, attorney from Zagreb, and together with me Mr. Kerns, attorney from the United States.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. Matthew Hennessy here for Mr. Naletilic with Chris Meek.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hennessy. I'm sorry the column gets into the way. Well, this may be perhaps the last Status Conference we will hear -- have in this appeal possibly. The last Status Conference was held in this case on the 17th of March, 2005. I don't think I have to remind the parties of the purposes of the Status Conferences. They are quite aware of the subjects that we are going to deal with in this case. But first let me ask the Appellants if they have any concerns relating to their detention conditions, to their health. Yes, Mr. Hennessy?

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. As to Mr. Naletilic, we have no concerns, nothing to report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the same applies to our client, no complaints or any particular issues to raise for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. If that's the case, we can move on to consider where we are with this appeal. First I would like to remind the parties that on the 6th of June, 2005 the Appeals Chamber issued a Scheduling Order setting the appeal hearings in this case for Monday through Wednesday, 17 to 19 October, 2005. I also want to note that the Prosecution has filed his seventh status report on the 12th of May, 2005. I wish to note that in that status report, if my understanding is correct, the Prosecutor communicated that Prosecution has completed its review of materials for purposes of disclosure to the Appellants, according to the Rule 68 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. KIND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Now, if that is the case, I would urge the Appellants to review the disclosed materials as expeditiously as possible. Perhaps I may inquire if they have -- how far are they with that review of the material disclosed by the Prosecution. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May it please the Court, Your Honour, we have -- the Registry finally allowed us some legal assistants who speak B/C/S and can read these documents, and they've already gone through their hours. We will have to speak with the Registry to try to get more hours. One is approximately 35 per cent finished with the EDS documents. Documents that have been in the Zagreb archives are being looked at and are about 40 per cent finished. And approximately, before July 4th, we had an e-mail from the Registry to all Defence counsel stating that there was new disclosures on the EDS system, and in looking through those it appears that some of those documents relate to our case. So we are working on it, Your Honour, and we hope to be able to get some more hours from the Registry so we can complete that task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. Anything for -- Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no particular problems concerning the nature of the documents and we will be prepared and ready on time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. So again, I will urge the Defence of Mr. Naletilic to review the materials as soon as possible, and if the case arises, to file motions as promptly as possible, in order that we can dispose of them in light of the appeals hearings next October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I just want to pose the question, Your Honour. May it please the Court, should the Registry not allow us any more hours, what do we do, because Mr. Hennessy and I cannot read B/C/S and we have to have somebody that's -- who can do that for us or the documents are meaningless. So I'm just posing the question to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: This is a question I cannot answer now, of course, but I will -- well, I will perhaps talk to the Registry myself and see how things may develop in this sense. Well, there is another issue I wanted to take up with the parties. On the 23rd of February this year, the parties were requested by me to file public versions of seven pleadings with International Tribunals. Now, the public versions of the Prosecution and Martinovic filings have been duly received. But we are still awaiting the filing of public versions of some filings by Mr. Naletilic. That is essentially the brief on appeal filed confidentially and under seal on the 15th of September, 2003, the revised brief of appeal of 10 October, and the reply to Prosecution's response on 17 November 2003. I would like to ask the Defence of Mr. Naletilic to file this public filings as soon as possible. And I would like to remind you, Mr. Hennessy, that any redaction to the filings should not alter the sequence of paragraphs and footnotes when you file the documents as public documents. I really would like to have this public versions soon. As soon as possible. What else? Well, I understand that there are no pending motions at this moment in the case, so there is nothing to deal with, with this. There are some decisions have been since the last Status Conference issued by the Appeals Chamber but the parties are of course aware of those decisions. I don't have to go back to them. Well, that's it, as far as I'm concerned. Are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise at this juncture? Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. KIND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No, the Prosecution has nothing further to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. The Appellants?

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Nothing for Mr. Naletilic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of Mr. Martinovic has nothing to raise either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. If that is so, I think we can adjourn this Status Conference. The Status Conference stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
